Fixed/Connections/broadband – FWA – 5G – share of FWA | Publication date: 24 September 2024 Based on historical data up to quarter 2 of 2024 | Share of all FWA broadband connections delivered over 5G.  Fixed-wireless access (FWA) is any wireless transmission technology that delivers connectivity from a fixed hub to distributed fixed points and serves principally as an alternative to wired fixed broadband. This excludes mobile broadband devices that enable seamless handover and other mobile devices such as Mi-Fi devices. The term 5G represents the globally agreed vision for “IMT2020” (the ITU's development of the next generation of mobile and wireless broadband connectivity). The mobile industry’s standards body, 3GPP, has completed the specifications for phase 1: full 5G New Radio (NR) standalone. Analysys Mason currently defines 5G as service of at least 1 Gbit/s per user, deployed for data networking or a low-latency service for IoT, that uses an extended range of spectrum bands (600–700 MHz and 3.5–70 GHz).  Connections metrics relate to the end-of-period figure.

Analysys Mason currently defines 5G as service of at least 1 Gbit/s per user, deployed for data networking or a low-latency service for IoT, that uses an extended range of spectrum bands (600–700 MHz and 3.5–70 GHz).
